scenario.prompt_to_agent:
After a configuration change window on router2, pc1 (195.11.14.2)
cannot reach pc2 (200.1.1.2) and pc2 cannot reach pc1. Both
routers are up, and the two ends of the inter-AS link still ping
each other directly (193.10.11.1 <-> 193.10.11.2), but the eBGP
session between router1 and router2 will not come up. Investigate.

injection.action: set a wrong remote-as (65001 instead of 1) on router2's neighbor statement for router1

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router2 BGP configuration (neighbor remote-as)
Mechanism: router2's config now says `neighbor 193.10.11.1
  remote-as 65001`, but router1 really is AS 1. During session
  setup router1's OPEN message carries AS 1; router2 compares it
  against the configured 65001, rejects the OPEN (bad peer AS
  notification), and the session never reaches Established. With
  no session, no prefixes are exchanged: router1 never learns
  200.1.1.0/24 and router2 never learns 195.11.14.0/24, so pc1 and
  pc2 cannot reach each other. The underlying link is healthy
  (direct pings across 193.10.11.0/24 work) and both daemons run.
Localization: router2
Root cause: wrong remote-as (65001 instead of 1) on router2's
  neighbor statement for 193.10.11.1
Fix: restore remote-as 1 on router2 (see [FIX])
scenario.fix_spec:
Restore the correct peer AS on router2:
`vtysh -c "configure terminal" -c "router bgp 2" -c "no neighbor 193.10.11.1" -c "neighbor 193.10.11.1 remote-as 1"`
The eBGP session establishes and the inter-AS prefixes are exchanged.
(A `service frr restart` on router2 also restores it, since /etc/frr/frr.conf
on disk was never modified.)

must-identify-mechanism: eBGP AS mismatch -- router1 is AS 1 but router2 expects 65001, so the session never establishes
bonus-rules-out-lower-layers: notes the inter-AS link and direct 193.10.11.1<->193.10.11.2 reachability are fine, isolating the fault to the BGP session configuration

agent.diagnosis_text:
The eBGP session is permanently stuck in Idle because router2 has a wrong
remote-AS configured for its neighbor 193.10.11.1 (router1). Router2's
running configuration shows:

    neighbor 193.10.11.1 remote-as 65001

But router1 is actually operating in AS 1. Every time router2 receives
router1's BGP OPEN message (which correctly advertises AS 1), router2
immediately rejects it and fires back a NOTIFICATION with error code
"OPEN Message Error / Bad Peer AS". This is confirmed by the neighbor
detail output on both sides: router2 shows "Notification sent (OPEN
Message Error/Bad Peer AS)" and has sent 4 NOTIFICATIONs while receiving
none; router1 shows "Notification received (OPEN Message Error/Bad Peer
AS)" with 8 NOTIFICATIONs received and connections established 1/dropped 1
(the only successful TCP handshake was immediately torn down). Because the
session never reaches ESTABLISHED, no prefixes are exchanged in either
direction — router1 cannot install 200.1.1.0/24 and router2 cannot install
195.11.14.0/24, making pc1 ↔ pc2 traffic blackholed at both routers. The
inter-AS link itself is healthy (L3 up, direct pings work), isolating the
fault entirely to the BGP control plane on router2.

Root cause: during the change window, the `remote-as` value for router1's
neighbor on router2 was incorrectly set to 65001 instead of 1.

Corrective fix: on router2, execute:
    configure terminal
    router bgp 2
    neighbor 193.10.11.1 remote-as 1
    end
    write memory
The session will come up on the next connect-retry (within ~4 seconds based
on current timer state).

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly names router2 as the device with the incorrect remote-as configuration and localizes the fault to router2.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-component: wrong remote-as (65001 instead of 1) on router2's neighbor statement for 193.10.11.1
per_axis.rationale: The submission explicitly identifies that router2's neighbor 193.10.11.1 is configured with remote-as 65001 instead of the correct AS 1.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-mechanism: eBGP AS mismatch -- router1 is AS 1 but router2 expects 65001, so the session never establishes
per_axis.rationale: The report clearly identifies an eBGP AS mismatch: router2 is configured with remote-as 65001 while router1 is AS 1, causing OPEN rejection (Bad Peer AS) and preventing session establishment.

per_axis.axis: bonus-rules-out-lower-layers: notes the inter-AS link and direct 193.10.11.1<->193.10.11.2 reachability are fine, isolating the fault to the BGP session configuration
per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly states the inter‑AS link is healthy and direct pings between 193.10.11.1 and 193.10.11.2 succeed, isolating the fault to the BGP control plane on router2.
The agent instructs changing router2's neighbor 193.10.11.1 to remote-as 1 (and saving), which directly fixes the incorrect peer AS and restores the eBGP session.

The investigation log contains direct outputs showing router2's neighbor configured with remote-as 65001, router1's local AS is 1, both neighbors are in Idle and no eBGP prefixes are learned — these observations support the diagnosis. The writeup adds some specific notification/ping details that are not fully present in the log, but the core causal chain (wrong remote-as → OPEN rejected → session Idle → no prefixes → reachability loss) is well supported.
